author: _alphafit
text:
Every “impossible” calisthenics move has an easier version hiding underneath it.

Master the progression, then earn the flex.

author: smartpostures
text:
1/10 — Band-assisted thoracic extension

This variation uses the bench to support the trunk while the band pulls across the upper arms and the hands stay behind the head.

The useful part is the combination of thoracic extension + shoulder positioning. You’re asking the upper back to extend while the shoulders stay active rather than simply forcing the chest upward.

The common mistake is getting the movement from the lower back instead. Keep the ribs controlled and let the upper back do more of the work.

This can be useful if you spend a lot of time flexed forward, but it isn’t a permanent “posture fix.”

author: postureuni
text:
Your Posture Needs Work‼️

These 5 resistance-band exercises target the muscles that help keep your shoulders and shoulder blades organized:

• Rhomboids + mid/lower traps • Rear delts • Lats • Scapular stabilizers • Upper-back endurance
✔️ Targets The Rhomboids & Mid/Lower Traps To Help Pull Your Shoulders Back
✔️ Strengthens The Rear Delts To Build Better Balance Around The Shoulder Joint
✔️ Activates The Lats & Improves Your Pulling Strength Without Heavy Weights
✔️ Trains The Smaller Stabilizing Muscles That Control Your Shoulder Blades

✔️ Builds Upper-Back Endurance To Help You Maintain Better Posture Throughout The Day

Hours of sitting, driving, and looking down at your phone can leave your chest feeling tight while your upper back does less work than it should.

That’s where these movements come in.

The goal isn't to force your shoulders backward all day.

It’s to build a back strong enough to support better positioning without constant effort.

Keep the reps slow. Control the band. Let the back—not the arms—do the work.

You don't need massive weights.

You need tension, control, and consistency.

author: postureuni
text:
Your shoulders don’t just need to be “strong.”

They need to know how to move, stabilize, and control the shoulder blade under load. 🧠

What caught my attention: the exercises aren’t simply about building bigger back muscles.

They challenge the muscles around the scapula, upper back, rear shoulder, and rotator cuff to work together.

That matters for swimmers, volleyball players, lifters—and anyone spending hours at a desk. 🏊‍♂️🏐🏋️‍♂️

It helps to 
✅ Improve shoulder mobility and stability 
✅ Strengthen the upper and mid-back muscles 
✅ Support better posture and spinal control 
✅ Reduce muscular overload and injury risk

⏱ How to perform: 
• 20-30 seconds per exercise
 • 2-3 sets 
• 2-3 times per week

The goal is having enough strength and control to move well through different positions.

Train the back.
Train the shoulder.
But most importantly: train the connection between them.

Tight hips make you slow and sore.

This is the reset.

Save this.

5-move hip medicine. Do it when you feel beat up.

👇

1. Rocking 90/90: 2x15
2. Single-leg RDL into hip gate: 2x10
3. Side lunge with iso hold: 2x12
4. Wall adductor opener: 2x1 min
5. Fire hydrant: 2x15
